proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_black_run_lt_start (a L : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a)
    (h : ∀ s ≤ L, centerColumn (a + s) = true) : L < a := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: While the centre column stays black, the cells immediately left of it at the run's own starting row are forced to alternate black-white-black, one cell deeper per further black step — that is `column_alternating_of_black_run`, already closed, read at the single-seed picture. The cone will not allow a deep checkerboard: at row `a` the two leftmost cells that exist at all, at `-a` and `-(a-1)`, are both black (`evolve_left_edge` and `evolve_left_second_diagonal`), while alternation says cells at consecutive depths are opposite. So the forced block cannot reach depth `a`, and therefore the run cannot last `a` further steps. `1 ≤ a` is needed and is not a technicality: the seed's own opening run at `a = 0` is two cells long, and there the cone's left edge and the origin are the same cell. Measured: 0 violations over 1,000,344 maximal runs to N = 2,000,000, and exactly tight at `a = 3`, where the run `111` at times 3, 4, 5 is the first non-trivial run there is (`explorer/p2seed_runs.mjs`). Orientation-sensitive: Talus measured that rule 86, rule 30 mirrored, has the same centre-column runs and fails the underlying alternation at 316 of 968 cells, so this is not a symmetric check.
proposals.disclaims: Nothing towards Prize 2 on its own. It bounds one run and says nothing about how often runs occur or about any density. Its only ingredient is the cone, and by Talus's fence (docs/attacks/2026-09-10-prize-2-s-residual-…, C2) the cone's sole consequence for the centre column is a run bound — every other local law rule 30 supplies is quantified over `Config` and so holds of every `Bool` sequence.

route.tactics:
by_contra hc
  have hc : a ≤ L := by omega
  have hcol : ∀ s ≤ L, column initialConfig 0 (a + s) = true := h
  have hedge := column_alternating_of_black_run initialConfig a L hcol a hc
  have hsec := column_alternating_of_black_run initialConfig a L hcol (a - 1) (by omega)
  rw [show column initialConfig (-(a : ℤ)) a = evolve a (-(a : ℤ)) from rfl,
    evolve_left_edge a] at hedge
  have h2 : evolve a (-((a - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) = true := by
    have hh := evolve_left_second_diagonal (a - 1)
    rwa [show a - 1 + 1 = a from by omega] at hh
  rw [show column initialConfig (-((a - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) a = evolve a (-((a - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) from rfl,
    h2] at hsec
  simp at hedge hsec
  omega

witness.expression:
(List.range 9).all fun a => (List.range 9).all fun L =>
  decide (a < 1) || decide (L < a) ||
    !((List.range (L + 1)).all fun s => centerColumn (a + s))
witness.range: a ≤ 8 and L ≤ 8. The cheap disjuncts come first so the automaton is evaluated only where the claim has content, at 1 ≤ a ≤ L, and the inner `all` stops at the first white cell — so no read goes past depth 12.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_white_run_lt_start (a L : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a)
    (h : ∀ s ≤ L, centerColumn (a + s) = false) : L < 3 * a := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The white twin of the black-run bound, and it splits on the colour of the column one cell left of the origin. That column is monotone inside a white run — once black it stays black, which is `white_run_forbidden`, closed — so let `t₀` be the row of the run where it turns black (or the row after the run, if it never does). Before `t₀` the centre and column `-1` are both white, and reading rule 30 backwards (`sideways_inverse` at `i = -j`) makes the next cell left white too, one deeper per row: an all-white triangle at row `a` of depth `t₀ - a`, which the black left edge at `-a` stops, giving `t₀ < 2 * a`. From `t₀` on, column `-1` is black under a white centre, and the same backwards reading forces the checkerboard with the *opposite* phase to a black run's — white at even depth, black at odd — to depth `a + L - t₀` at row `t₀`, which the cone's two adjacent black cells at `-t₀` and `-(t₀-1)` stop, giving `a + L < 2 * t₀ + 2`. Substituting the first into the second gives `L < 3 * a`. Measured: both forced patterns hold with 0 failures over 7,521 maximal white runs to row 30,000, and `t₀ / a` never exceeds 1.167 (`explorer/p2seed_white.mjs`). The conclusion is far from tight — over 2,000,000 rows every maximal white run beginning at `a ≥ 1` satisfies `length ≤ a`, worst ratio 0.5 (`explorer/p2seed_runs.mjs`) — and `3` is stated because `3` is what this argument gives.
proposals.disclaims: Not the sharp bound, and nothing here explains the gap: measured, a maximal white run beginning at `a` has length at most `a/2`, where this proves only `< 3a`. Nothing towards Prize 2 on its own.

witness.expression:
(List.range 6).all fun a => (List.range 16).all fun L =>
  decide (a < 1) || decide (L < 3 * a) ||
    !((List.range (L + 1)).all fun s => !centerColumn (a + s))
witness.range: a ≤ 5 and L ≤ 15. Weak on purpose: with the cheap disjuncts first, the automaton is read only where `L ≥ 3a`, and the white stretch there breaks within a cell or two, so nothing deep is checked. The bound's content is at larger `a` and is covered by the scripts named in the reason, not by this.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_window_not_constant (a : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) :
    (∃ s ≤ 3 * a, centerColumn (a + s) = true) ∧
      (∃ s ≤ 3 * a, centerColumn (a + s) = false) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The two run bounds read as one statement about a window: from time `a` to time `4 * a` the centre column is neither all black nor all white. All black would make the first `a + 1` cells of the window a black stretch, contradicting `centerColumn_black_run_lt_start` at `L = a`; all white would make all `3 * a + 1` of them a white stretch, contradicting `centerColumn_white_run_lt_start` at `L = 3 * a`. Stated with the same `3 * a` on both sides so the counting node has one window to work with rather than two. This is the interface: it is the form in which rule 30 says something about the centre column that a `Bool` sequence can fail, and the next node is the only thing that consumes it.
proposals.disclaims: Nothing towards Prize 2: it is the two run bounds restated. The window is far too wide — measured, every window `[a, 2a]` already holds both colours — and the width is the white bound's constant rather than a fact about the picture.

witness.expression:
(List.range 5).all fun a =>
  decide (a < 1) ||
    (((List.range (3 * a + 1)).any fun s => centerColumn (a + s)) &&
      ((List.range (3 * a + 1)).any fun s => !centerColumn (a + s)))
witness.range: 1 ≤ a ≤ 4. `any` stops at the first witness of each colour and both are found within two cells of `a` at every `a` in range, so no read goes past depth 6.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumnCount_ge_of_pow (n : ℕ) :
    n ≤ ((Finset.range (5 ^ n)).filter fun t => centerColumn t = true).card ∧
      n ≤ ((Finset.range (5 ^ n)).filter fun t => centerColumn t = false).card := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The windows `[5 ^ k, 5 ^ (k+1))` for `k < n` are disjoint and together cover `[1, 5 ^ n)`, and each one contains the window `[5 ^ k, 4 * 5 ^ k]` that `centerColumn_window_not_constant` says holds both colours — `4 * 5 ^ k < 5 ^ (k+1)` is the whole reason the base is 5 rather than 4. So each colour picks up at least one new cell per power of 5, and by induction on `n` both counts below `5 ^ n` are at least `n`. This is the first bound on the centre column's excess that uses rule 30 at all: it gives `|2 * count N - N| ≤ N - 2 * ⌊log₅ N⌋`, where `centerColumn_density_tendsto_half_iff_excess_nat` — the ℕ form of the prize, already closed — says exactly that the same quantity is eventually below `N / d` for every `d`. So it lands in the residual's own vocabulary and in the same inequality, at a strength that is not remotely enough. The derivation was checked in Lean with the window statement taken in as a hypothesis rather than assumed available (`explorer/p2seed_scratch.lean`, builds clean), so what is proposed here is what its consumer needs and not merely something true.
proposals.disclaims: Nothing towards Prize 2, and the gap is not a matter of sharpening. The bound is `N - 2 log₅ N`, which is `N(1 - o(1))`, where the prize needs `o(N)`; Talus's attack of 2026-09-10 shows the whole run route is capped at `N(1 - 1/(c log N))` for any run bound however sharp, so no successor of these four nodes reaches it. What it does is put one statement about `centerColumnCount` on the board that a `Bool` sequence can fail — all twelve closed P2 nodes hold of every `ℕ → Bool`, which is the measurement that named this tier.

witness.expression:
(List.range 2).all fun n =>
  decide (n ≤ ((Finset.range (5 ^ n)).filter fun t => centerColumn t = true).card) &&
    decide (n ≤ ((Finset.range (5 ^ n)).filter fun t => centerColumn t = false).card)
witness.range: n < 2, and I want to be plain that this is nearly vacuous: it checks the shape of the inequality and the colours are not swapped, and nothing else. `n = 2` needs `centerColumn 24`, which is depth 24 against a usable ceiling near 18, so this claim cannot carry a naive witness that reaches its content. The content was checked in the engine instead: both counts below `5 ^ n` exceed `n` by orders of magnitude at every `n ≤ 8` (`explorer/p2seed_runs.mjs` prints the same tally in base 2).
